newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, in turnabout, allows archaeological dig.
newsitem.headline: France, in turnabout, allows archaeological dig.

text.p: The French government, in a face-saving change of heart, on Thursday temporarily halted a construction project in the southern town of Rodez so that archaeologists could first examine Roman ruins on the site.
But local archaeologists accused the government of half-hearted measures and threatened to go on strike or occupy government offices in protest.

Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy said archaeologists would be given two months and 600,000 francs ($108,000), half of it from his ministry, to examine the Rodez ruins, which could be as much as 2,000 years old.
In a statement, he said that Prime Minister Alain Juppe wanted to remind all local officials of the need to protect France's archaeological heritage.
Culture Ministry unions had threatened a strike earlier in the week after Douste-Blazy announced that the construction project was to go ahead despite the finding of Roman remains.
The unions had made public a November 12 letter from Juppe dismissing the need for an archaeological dig in Rodez.

Despite the concessions, state archaeologists in the region called on other archaeologists, students and researchers to renew their protests by either going on strike or occupying regional offices of the Culture Ministry in nearby Toulouse.
They called on the state to provide greater funding for digs and bolster rules protecting historical sites.
